Shinji Mikami to join AIAS Hall of Fame at 2026 DICE Awards

News
Shinji Mikami to join AIAS Hall of Fame at 2026 DICE Awards
Goichi Suda will be presenting the award to the Resident Evil director.
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 16, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Shinji Mikami photograph provided by AIAS
The prolific game developer and one of the pioneers of the Resident Evil series, Shinji Mikami, will receive the Hall of Fame Award at the 30th annual DICE Awards ceremony on February 18 of next year.
As announced today by the
Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences (AIAS)
, Mikami, current creative director and CEO of Unbound, will be honored for his career in the game industry, which has spanned over 30 years.
Grasshopper Manufacture CEO and lead game designer Goichi Suda, best known as Suda 51, will be presenting the award. Suda and Mikami previously worked together on the likes of
Killer7
and
Shadows of the Damned.
"It was from Mikami-san that I learned how to approach game development, both as a director and as a designer," Suda said in the announcement. "Of all the many Padawans Mikami-san has mentored, I'm truly honored that I was chosen to be his presenter for this induction into a kind of video game hall-of-fame. As one such Padawan, please allow me to celebrate my Obi-Wan Kenobi, Shinji Mikami, through this honorable award. I'm sure Mikami-san's innumerable fans and industry comrades are just as delighted as I am to see him receive such an amazing award."

"Shinji Mikami is a monumental and influential figure for both fans and developers alike," AIAS president Meggan Scavio said. "He has continually demonstrated his originality and creative vision that resonates and inspires the action game genre. We are honored to be able to celebrate Mikami-san's achievements and induct him into our Hall of Fame during our 30th anniversary of the DICE Awards."
Mikami founded and led
The Evil Within
and
Hi-Fi Rush
developer Tango Gameworks, but
made for the exit
before the studio was sold
to Krafton by Microsoft
. He then established Unbound towards the end of 2022.
Early this year,
Stellar Blade
developer
Shift Up acquired Unbound
for an undisclosed fee. The company said the move is intended to expand Unbound's publishing footprint while bolstering its development capabilities with "world class" talent.
The DICE Awards, and Mikami's induction into the AIAS Hall of Fame, will air on Thursday, February 18.
